From 4b5d099e1049909a16e93648d80df18a516afb73 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jonathan McPherson <jonathan@rstudio.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Dec 2017 14:58:50 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] save console process before computing interaction mode; fixes
 #1810

this change fixes an issue; because getInteractionMode()
uses the saved console process, it needs to be set before we check the
interaction mode.

diff --git a/src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/vcs/common/ConsoleProgressDialog.java b/src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/vcs/common/ConsoleProgressDialog.java
index dbedddd688..0e5b0af8e6 100644
--- a/src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/vcs/common/ConsoleProgressDialog.java
+++ b/src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/vcs/common/ConsoleProgressDialog.java
@@ -76,6 +76,9 @@ public class ConsoleProgressDialog extends ProgressDialog
          throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                "Invalid combination of arguments to ConsoleProgressDialog");
       }
+
+      // save console process so that we can compute interaction mode below
+      consoleProcess_ = consoleProcess;
       
       if (getInteractionMode() != ConsoleProcessInfo.INTERACTION_NEVER)
       {
-- 
2.48.1

## Summary

**File modified:** `src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/vcs/common/ConsoleProgressDialog.java`

**Modification:** In the constructor, the assignment `consoleProcess_ = consoleProcess;` was moved earlier, now occurring right before the call to `getInteractionMode()` instead of after it (presumably it was previously set later in the constructor).

**Relationship:** This is a single-file fix addressing an ordering bug within the same method. The method `getInteractionMode()` relies on the instance field `consoleProcess_` to determine the interaction mode of the console process. Previously, `consoleProcess_` was assigned *after* `getInteractionMode()` was called, meaning the field was still null (or stale) when the interaction mode was computed, leading to incorrect behavior (issue #1810). By moving the assignment of `consoleProcess_` before the `getInteractionMode()` call, the method now has access to the correct, up-to-date console process reference, ensuring the interaction mode check functions correctly.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
`if (getInteractionMode() != ConsoleProcessInfo.INTERACTION_NEVER)`
`attachToProcess(consoleProcess);` (which presumably sets `consoleProcess_ = consoleProcess;` too late, after `getInteractionMode()` is already called)
Reason: `getInteractionMode()` relies on the field `consoleProcess_` to compute the interaction mode, but this field was only assigned later in the constructor (via `attachToProcess(consoleProcess)`), so when `getInteractionMode()` was called, `consoleProcess_` was still null, causing it to return an incorrect interaction mode.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
`consoleProcess_ = consoleProcess;`
Reason: By assigning `consoleProcess_` immediately after the null-check and before calling `getInteractionMode()`, the method now has access to the correct `consoleProcess` reference when computing the interaction mode, ensuring the dialog's behavior (read-only vs. interactive, history enabled/disabled) is based on the actual process's interaction mode rather than a null/default value.
